questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Location and country

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Amazing experience! Wish everyone could do this

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Yes, almost anything was on UCSB Gold which was nice. It would have been nice to have a designated student to talk to who could tell about the social life and hear about events and clubs going on. Really, anything not school related.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an introduction event, the first friday of the quarter.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I think it would have been easy enough, you just have to start looking several month in advance. I was too late for that

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Find private housing!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The facilities and location were good, but didnt like my house mates, and it was kind of difficult to be relocated.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You need to cantact the professor for every single class to get prerequsites for any class you want to take. This takes time so you have to begin before your sign-up time. This would have been nice to know.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You get 3 sign-up slots in which you can sign up for classes. Since there is a fixed amount spots, you need to have all prerequsites ready and be ready right when it is your turn, if you want to get into a popular class.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I dont know

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had a few problems finding classes bacause they were either to easy or to difficult. I ended up with a good schedule.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to get your prerequsites fixed early. Furthermore, you can sign up for more classes than you intend to take and drop them after the quarter starts.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took some easier classes (lower divsion), and some more advanced classes (upper division). The more advanced classes might be slightly easier then the ones I would be taken at home, but since I didnt know a lot of people to discuss it with, I think it worked out for the best.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The professors seem more invested in there students and host weekly office hours. They did have attendence and more quizzes which I didnt like.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to Pshycology
Probability and Statistics B
Advanced Linear Algebra
Dinosaurs
Principles of Data Science
Probability and Statistics C

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Advanced Linear Algebra (MATH 108B) - I dont think we have anything similar on KU. Very work heavy though.
Introdution to Psychology - Easy but interesting.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You have to buy American approved health insurance. If you buy the school insurance, it is 1000 dollars pr quarter, thus 2000 dollars. I paid 600 dollars for ISO health insurance for 6 month. Your danish travel insurance is not good enough.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is expensive. Puplic transport was free in Santa Barbara with student card.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not a lot of clubs, but a lot of other social stuff going on. Consider joining the excursion club.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Buy a car and travel.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to national parks and Mexico

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Americans are very open - everyone you have meet just a few times are considered your friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Just a lot of minor differences

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Social life is not just limited to the weekends

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Buy a car, travel and join the excursion club

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Join the excursion club

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing the culture

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting Americans to understand why Im 24 and havent graduated yet. they are a lot younger over there.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Nope

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
